definitions.explanation: The second day of the weekend and traditionally a day of rest. The kanji 日 means 'sun,' similar to how 'Sunday' derives from 'Sun day' in English.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{日曜日|にちようび}です。
{日曜日|にちようび}は{休|やす}みです。
{日曜日|にちようび}に{家族|かぞく}と{出|で}かけます。
examples.english: I go out with my family on Sunday.

examples.japanese: {毎週|まいしゅう}{日曜日|にちようび}は{家|いえ}でゆっくりします。
examples.english: Every Sunday, I relax at home.

examples.japanese: {日曜日|にちようび}に{友達|ともだち}と{公園|こうえん}で{遊|あそ}んでから、{一緒|いっしょ}に{晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べました。
examples.english: On Sunday, I played with friends at the park and then we ate dinner together.

notes:
{日曜日|にちようび} means "Sunday." The kanji {日|にち} means "sun," paralleling the English "Sunday."

DAYS OF THE WEEK PATTERN:
All days use 〜{曜日|ようび}:
- {日曜日|にちようび}: Sunday (sun)
- {月曜日|げつようび}: Monday (moon)
- {火曜日|かようび}: Tuesday (fire/Mars)
- {水曜日|すいようび}: Wednesday (water/Mercury)
- {木曜日|もくようび}: Thursday (wood/Jupiter)
- {金曜日|きんようび}: Friday (gold/Venus)
- {土曜日|どようび}: Saturday (earth/Saturn)

ABBREVIATION: Can be shortened to {日曜|にちよう}.

CULTURAL NOTE: In Japan, Sunday is typically a rest day spent with family or relaxing before the work week.
